title: Confirmed clearing inside a delivered plot
why: The alert is dated after the EUDR cutoff, has the highest confidence, and falls directly inside P-029, which supplied cocoa to ChocoDurable in 2025. The evidence directly links post-cutoff forest clearing to a delivered plot, so the promise cannot hold for the entire supply.

title: High-confidence alert before the cutoff
why: The added alert predates 31 December 2020 and therefore does not establish clearing after the regulatory cutoff. Nothing in this change contradicts the promise, and the base world's deliveries remain traced to geolocated plots.

title: Strong alert just outside the plot
why: The alert is recent and highly confident, but its reported location is 15 metres beyond the plot boundary rather than inside the delivered plot. The proximity warrants further investigation, but the available evidence does not establish that forest was cleared within the company's supplied plot.

title: Missing alert source
why: The investigation cannot retrieve satellite alerts, so it cannot establish whether relevant post-cutoff clearing occurred on delivered plots. Existing registry and delivery records remain available, but the missing evidence prevents a defensible conclusion that the promise holds.

title: Supplier deliveries without registered plots
why: F-002 continues supplying cocoa, but its deliveries can no longer be traced to registered geolocated plots. Because the company promises traceability for every tonne, the investigation cannot verify the complete supply or conclude that deforestation occurred.

title: Untraced cocoa hidden in certified volume
why: The additional 2.5 tonnes have no linked plot, so they violate the claim that every tonne is traced to a geolocated farm. Sustainability certification does not identify the missing production location or establish that the untraced cocoa is deforestation-free.

title: Low-confidence alert alone
why: The alert is inside a delivered plot and postdates the cutoff, but its low confidence does not meet the company's stated threshold for a confirmed alert. With no other contradictory evidence introduced, the promise holds on the evidence checked, although the low-confidence signal may justify additional monitoring.

title: Delivered plot moved away from its alert
why: Moving P-029 substantially changes the registered location used to associate its deliveries with satellite evidence. Without evidence establishing which location is correct, the investigator cannot reliably match alerts to the actual producing farm or validate its geolocation.

title: Forest clearing allegation in an NGO note

changes.text: During a visit in May 2025, our investigators observed forest clearing within the boundaries of plot P-029, which is registered to supplier F-031 and supplied to ChocoDurable SA.

why: The added NGO statement attributes post-cutoff clearing to a delivered plot, but the note alone does not provide independently corroborated geospatial observations or supporting evidence sufficient to establish the event conclusively. The allegation must be investigated against plot boundaries, field records, and satellite imagery before accusing the supplier.

title: Point geolocation hides the precise boundary
why: P-029 is declared as a point with an area of 5 hectares, so its boundary must be inferred from the declared area rather than verified from a supplied polygon. The high-confidence alert lies just beyond that inferred boundary, leaving insufficient evidence to attribute the clearing to the delivered plot without better geolocation or field verification.
